title: ECDC: DRC Ebola Toll Rises to 7,890 Cases, 3,799 Deaths as Contact Tracing Rebounds to 83.4%
detail: The ECDC's Ebola outbreak tracker, published 25 September 2026 at 16:05 CEST with data through 23 September, put DRC's confirmed toll at 7,890 cases and 3,799 deaths — up from 7,773 cases and 3,759 deaths in the prior (21 September) report, a rise of 117 cases and 40 deaths. Ituri remains the epicenter with 6,032 cases and 2,764 deaths across 28 of 36 health zones, followed by North Kivu with 1,480 cases and 884 deaths across 16 of 34 zones (a crude provincial case-fatality rate of roughly 59.7%). Haut-Uélé (322 cases/130 deaths, 7 of 13 zones), Tshopo (43/15, 7 of 23), Bas-Uélé (8/4, 3 of 11), South Kivu (3/1, 1 of 34) and Sud-Ubangi (2/1, 1 of 16) round out the seven affected provinces, with the outbreak still spanning 63 of 167 mapped health zones. National contact-tracing coverage rebounded to 83.4% of identified contacts, up from 79.9% in the 19 September report, continuing the metric's week-to-week volatility. The update recorded 893 patients currently hospitalized in isolation and 1,966 cumulative recoveries, for a crude national case fatality rate of roughly 48.2% — essentially unchanged from the prior report despite the continued rise in absolute numbers. The report comes two days after a US-convened G20+ Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New York mobilized roughly $2.9 billion in international commitments toward the response.

title: WHO: Ebola Spreads to Two More Health Zones Bordering South Sudan and CAR; Africa CDC Flags Massive Contact-Tracing Shortfall
detail: WHO's Disease Outbreak News update, published 25 September 2026, confirmed the Bundibugyo virus outbreak has expanded to two additional health zones since the 11 September update: Bulu in Sud-Ubangi province (bordering the Central African Republic) and Dungu in Haut-Uélé province (bordering South Sudan). This brings the total to 63 affected health zones across seven provinces, and WHO said explicitly that 'this latest geographic expansion increases the risk of cross-border transmission,' rating the risk to countries sharing a land border with DRC as high. As of 23 September, DRC had recorded 7,890 confirmed cases and 3,799 deaths (CFR 48.1%), with 1,966 recoveries. WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said 'it's very difficult to see Ebola in isolation because even our response to Ebola is affected by the conflict,' citing displacement and access constraints from the M23/FARDC fighting in the Kivus. Separately, Africa CDC Director-General Dr. Jean Kaseya disclosed a severe contact-tracing shortfall: with more than 7,000 cases, roughly 420,000 contacts should exist under standard ratios, yet only about 30,000 are currently being tracked — a small fraction of ECDC's separately reported 83.4% national contact-tracing coverage figure, which measures follow-up only among contacts that have actually been identified. Kaseya said 'when the outbreak is at community level, we cannot talk about control.' The Bundibugyo species has no approved vaccine or treatment, though a Phase 3 Ervebo cross-protection trial is underway in Ituri.

title: Mpox Case Confirmed in Bunia, the Epicenter of DRC's Ebola Outbreak
detail: A laboratory confirmed a case of mpox in Bunia, Ituri — the epicenter of DRC's Ebola outbreak — on Friday 25 September 2026, per Reuters. A 21-year-old woman admitted to hospital Thursday with lesions consistent with mpox tested positive the next day; a second suspected case, a 32-year-old woman, awaited lab results, and five suspected mpox cases in Bunia were under investigation in total. Dr. Adelard Lofungola, a health official who served as deputy incident manager for DRC's mpox response, said the Ebola outbreak's strain on the health system was complicating efforts to monitor other infections, and that mpox activity has increased in several parts of the country over the past month. DRC had declared an end to mpox as a national public health emergency in April 2026 after a three-year outbreak with more than 34,000 confirmed cases nationwide. The finding raises the prospect of a second hemorrhagic/vesicular disease circulating simultaneously in the same city (Bunia has 7,890 Ebola cases and 3,799 deaths recorded nationally as of 23 September).
